Program Prerequisites and How to Apply
On December 16, 2025 President Trump issued an expanded travel ban, restricting entry of nationals from 20 additional countries, including the Palestinian Authority, and limiting exceptions included in the prior ban.
Due to these new restrictions, prospective students who are citizens of one of the listed countries and who are currently residing outside of the U.S., are now barred from entering the U.S. to study and attend classes. As a result, KU Medical Center is no longer able to offer admission to these individuals, and they should not apply at this time.
If a prospective student from one of the listed countries is currently residing in the U.S., they may apply for admission.
Any questions related to this travel entry ban can be directed to kconnelly@kumc.edu.
The application portal for Fall 2027 matriculation is now open, with applications due December 1st, 2026. All required application materials must be received by December 15th, 2026. Once your completed application has been received it will be reviewed by the admissions committee. For select applicants who currently reside in the United States or Canada, we will hold our Recruitment Weekend on February 26th through February 28th, 2027. Select International applicants will be interviewed via telephone or Zoom. All decisions regarding interviews and acceptance to the program will be made as soon as possible, but no later than April.
Program Prerequisites Include:
B.S. or B.A. degree
One year of general chemistry
One year of organic chemistry or one semester of organic chemistry and one semester of biochemistry
One year of biological sciences
One semester of calculus
One semester of physics
To Apply for Admission:
Click here to submit your application, and pay the $60 non-refundable application fee. The academic program to be selected is "Biomedical Sciences (PhD)". You will be asked to provide contact e-mail addresses for three references. After you submit your application, your references will then receive an automated e-mail with instructions for submitting their letter of recommendation through our online system.
Scanned unofficial copies of transcripts can be uploaded with your application materials for the review process. However, if you are accepted, please request that one copy of your official transcripts from each college/university previously attended be sent to the Interdisciplinary Graduate Program in Biomedical Sciences at the address below or via email to igpbs@kumc.edu using one of the transcript clearinghouses:
Interdisciplinary Graduate Program in Biomedical Sciences
MS 3025
3901 Rainbow Blvd
Kansas City, KS 66160
Applicants with transcripts from an international institution may submit an unofficial Foreign Credential Evaluation (FCE) report during the application review process. However, if an applicant with transcripts from an international institution does matriculate into the program, they are required to order a FCE report from a recognized FCE company. Please review the requirements on the International Transcripts Need Foreign Credential Evaluation (FCE) Reports page.
Resume/CV
Personal statement which includes your background, why you need a PhD to achieve your career goals, and how the IGPBS and KUMC can help you achieve these goals. Research statement which describes your research activities. Each document should be no more than two pages single spaced.
If you are an international student that is required to submit a TOEFL score (not a native-speaker of English and country of citizenship is not on the TOEFL Exempt List), request an official copy of your TOEFL scores be sent to KUMC. Minimum TOEFL scores for admission are at least a 23 on the Reading and Listening portions of the TOEFL IBT and at least a 19 on the Writing section. For the New TOEFL test, the overall minimum is 4.5, with no section below 4.0. We do accept IELTS, GATEWAY, and Duolingo scores in place of the TOEFL. Minimum scores for the IELTS are 6.5 overall with no part score below 6; Minimum GATEWAY scores are 475 overall, and the Writing section minimum of 425; Minimum Duolingo scores are 115 overall, with no part below 100. Either the TOEFL, IELTS, GATEWAY, or Duolingo must have been taken within two years of the first semester of enrollment.
For direct reporting of TOEFL scores, our institution code is 6895.
